posts.title_en: I datamined the Guild Conquest boss
posts.summary_en: First pass at a boss datamine: the boss's damage reduction (피감) runs through 6 stages, 10/20/30/50/90/99%, so the OP reasons the first 12 s should carry maximum damage. A commenter notes the per-stage score multiplier also differs and most of a run's score still lands mid-fight. Superseded/refined by the same author's dc:71383.
mechanics: Boss damage reduction (피감) has 6 stages: 10%, 20%, 30%, 50%, 90%, 99% (first draft; see dc:71383 for the revised numbers with an added timing schedule).
Commenter: the score multiplier differs by stage, and in practice most points are still earned mid-fight, not in the opening seconds.
disagreements: OP's stage list (10/20/30/50/90/99) differs slightly from the same author's later post dc:71383 (10/30/50/70/90/99); treat the later post as the corrected version.

quotes.en: The damage reduction runs stage 1 to 6 as 10/20/30/50/90/99%.

posts.title_en: The Guild Conquest boss's damage reduction rises over time
posts.summary_en: The same author as dc:67285/67299 posts a refined datamine: boss damage reduction runs through 6 stages (10/30/50/70/90/99%) starting at 0% at fight start, upgrading first at 10s elapsed then every 12s after; boss ATK (offense stat) also jumps by orders of magnitude at each of the same stage boundaries. The 99% stage is never reached because the fight is only 60s long. This is the single most load-bearing (if unverified) post for the fight's difficulty curve.
mechanics: Boss damage reduction (defense side): starts at 0% (elapsed 0-10s), then 10% (10-22s), 30% (22-34s), 50% (34-46s), 70% (46-58s), 90% (58s+); a 99% stage exists in the data but is never reached in a 60s fight.

Boss ATK (offense side) at each of those same stage boundaries: 5000 -> 505,000 -> 2,500,500 -> 12,500,500 -> 250,005,000 -> 750,005,000 -> 1,562,505,000. Boss DEF is stated fixed at 2000 throughout (matches dc:67299's earlier figure).
Poster's own confusion: doesn't know why a 99% DR / final-ATK stage exists in the table if the fight is capped at 60s — speculates a future time-limit extension.
disagreements: The DR stage values here (10/30/50/70/90/99) differ slightly from the same author's first draft in dc:67285 (10/20/30/50/90/99); this post is the later, more detailed one and includes a timing schedule the first one lacked.

quotes.kr: 피감은 단계마다 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, 99% ... 방어력은 2000고정, 시작피감은 0% 10초부터 강화되서 12초마다 올라감 근데 마지막 단계는 토벌전이 60초라 적용이 안되긴함
quotes.en: DR per stage is 10/30/50/70/90/99%... DEF is fixed at 2000, starting DR is 0%; it upgrades starting at 10s and every 12s after. But the last stage never applies since Guild Conquest is 60s.

posts.title_en: Found a way to always push Milk to the front
posts.summary_en: Removing every backline support/healer (Herb, Rockstar, Lime, Angel, bird-pet-cookie etc, or setting their power to Lv.1 so they can't spawn) forces Milk to charge all the way to melee contact with the boss, because nothing is left behind her to stop the advance. Confirms formation resolves as a straight run-in that stops on first blocking ally/collision, not a scripted stop point; over-optimizing it can wipe the team too early, capping score.
mechanics: Cookie run-in behaviour: with no cookies left behind a given unit, it keeps advancing until it reaches the boss/front; formation is a physical run-in-and-collide process, not fixed stop points.

Killing the formation puzzle too well (everyone reaches an ideal position) can cause the team to engage/die too early in the fight, which caps total score even though positioning looks perfect — survival duration and positioning both matter for score.

posts.title_en: RIP Panda Dumpling, you served well
posts.summary_en: Retirement thread for Panda Dumpling now that Candy Shade Pouch exists. Images (transcribed) give exact pet values: Panda Dumpling at 9★ gives allies +18% lift resist and +70 flat HP to support-type cookies; Candy Shade Pouch at 5★(SSR) gives allies +22.5% lift resist / +7.5% max HP, plus +1.70% Water-element damage as an owned-cookie bonus. Commenters report Candy Shade Pouch capping at +30% lift resist / +7.5% HP at 10-14★ — the +7.5% HP cap contradicts mechanics.json's existing '+12.5% HP max' claim for this pet.
mechanics: Panda Dumpling (9★, image-verified): party-wide +18% lift resistance ('동행 효과'); +70 flat HP to support-type cookies owned ('보유 효과').
Candy Shade Pouch (5★ SSR, image-verified): party-wide +22.5% lift resistance, +7.5% max HP; +1.70% Water-element damage as an owned-cookie bonus.

Commenters (10-14★, unverified by image): Candy Shade Pouch caps at +30% lift resistance and +7.5% max HP — NOTE this HP figure (7.5%) conflicts with the existing dashboard mechanics.json entry of '+12.5% HP max' for this pet; the 5★ HP number (7.5%) matches the higher-star reports exactly, suggesting HP may not scale further past 5★ and the 12.5% figure should be rechecked.

Charge-type (돌격형) cookies are avoided in Guild Conquest specifically because they physically rush to melee range on the boss, breaking the tuned line formation and usually missing Milk's ATK-buff range.

timeline.detail: Guild Conquest fight lasts 60 s total, confirmed independently by crumb.gg's DPS chart page ('Fight length 60 s', evidence/15-crumbgg/32-dps-read.txt) and by a datamine poster ('토벌전이 60초', dc:71383). The in-run HUD timer counts down from 60 to 0 (dc:69724, prior evidence); '17초' and '30초' in community shorthand are both remaining-time marks, i.e. elapsed 43 s and elapsed 30 s respectively.

Team runs in from starting positions and collides into a line; there is no scripted stop point; a cookie keeps advancing until physically blocked by an ally or the boss, so leftover move-speed stats or missing backline units change where the line settles (dc:72759, dc:74804; prior evidence dc:60340, dc:64839).

Per an unverified single-author datamine (dc:67285, refined in dc:71383): boss damage reduction is 0% and boss ATK is at its base value (5000) for the first 10 s. This is the highest-damage-efficiency window of the fight, before the boss starts scaling up its own mitigation and offense.
Datamine claim: boss DR steps to 10% and boss ATK jumps to 505,000 at 10 s elapsed. DEF stays fixed at 2000 throughout (matches the independent DEF figure in dc:67299 by the same author).
Datamine claim: DR steps to 30%, boss ATK to 2,500,500.

A distinct sub-event around 27 s remaining, separate from the 30 s slam: thrown mobs ('쫄') self-destruct near the front line. A fully-built (Lv.100) Dark Choco was reported dying to this specifically, while a Lv.1 Dark Choco instead died to the 30 s slam itself (dc:71219); matches the '3 bomb mobs thrown at the front line' step of the previously-recorded 30 s sequence (dc:53667, prior evidence).

The '30 s slam' ('30초 쿵'/'30초 내려찍기'/'부랄찢기'): the boss's first major team-wide hit. Prior evidence (dc:53667) describes the full sequence as gift-bomb -> ground pounds -> 3 bomb-mobs thrown at the front line -> jump. This batch adds concrete HP survival floors (~3-4M HP generally, front row ~4.5M / back row ~3.5M as a more granular split) and a team-power curve (~400M power = 1-2 survivors, ~600M = full survival, ~1.5G = never dies here). It is RNG-sensitive even at fixed power/build (one account cleared it on a 3rd retry after 2 failures at identical build). Milk is disproportionately likely to die here because she is healing others during this window without being healed herself, which then removes her ATK buff for the remainder of the fight.
Datamine claim: DR steps to 50%, boss ATK to 12,500,500. This bracket covers the 30 s slam window through the run-up to the 17 s wipe.

Cookies begin dying individually starting around 19 s remaining (elapsed ~41 s) — the wipe is a taper, not a single simultaneous kill. Dead cookies remain visible in the formation UI with a greyed portrait and an hourglass badge rather than disappearing; no evidence of in-run revival was found (searches for '부활' turned up only unrelated gacha-cookie discussion).

The '17 s super-jump' (elapsed 43 s): historically a certain full-team wipe ('확정전멸') for every publicly documented run through at least late September, including runs at 2.2G team power (dc:69250) and the #1 guild's own 827G video (prior evidence). The first credible survival reports appear only at very high account power (~21G, dc:76583, prior evidence), and only for 4 of 12 cookies (Macaron/Brightseeker/Pomegranate/Skating Queen), who then keep dealing damage until about 8 s remain. This remains a timing correlation with the Season 5 score jump, not a shown, replicated build.
Datamine claim: DR steps to 70%, boss ATK to 250,005,000.
Datamine claim: DR steps to 90%, boss ATK to 750,005,000, for the final ~2 s of the fight.

The 60 s timer, not a team wipe, ends the fight and locks the score. A team that wipes completely well before 60 s still keeps whatever damage it dealt before dying (a full wipe at the 30 s slam still scored >100x in one report) — there is no bonus or penalty tied to surviving to the buzzer beyond the extra damage window that survival buys.

The datamine's implied 7th stage (99% DR, boss ATK 1,562,505,000, which would start at elapsed 70 s) is never reached inside a 60 s fight. The original poster has no explanation for why the data table extends past the fight's own time limit — flagged as an open question for a client datamine (is there an unused 'overtime' mode, or is this a leftover/placeholder stage).

boss.hp: Unverified single-source datamine claims boss HP ~2^62 (~4.6×10^18); functionally this plus the fixed 60 s clock and the escalating DR schedule mean the encounter is a pure damage race, not a depletable-HP kill — no source anywhere claims the boss can be brought to 0 HP or that doing so changes the outcome.
boss.defense: Claimed fixed DEF 2000 throughout the fight (two independent posts by the same author agree on this number, dc:67299 and dc:71383); damage reduction (a separate, time-gated stat) instead ramps from 0% to 90%+ across 6 stages timed off elapsed seconds (see timeline). Accuracy and focus/resist are reported as unnecessary against this boss (prior evidence, dc:43653, dc:71381): crit resistance does nothing and the boss has low evasion/resist.
boss.attack: Claimed boss ATK stat scales by orders of magnitude at each of the same DR stage boundaries (5,000 at phase 0 up to 750,005,000 at phase 5), which is offered as the likely reason the 30 s and 17 s patterns hit so much harder than earlier chip damage.
boss.movement_targeting: No source in this batch describes the boss moving toward or selecting individual cookie targets; damage appears to land on the team's front line/whoever is in range rather than a single chased target. Open question for a datamine.
boss.lift_and_cc: The boss can lift/launch cookies airborne (에어본); lift resistance (띄우기 저항) on the ally side is what prevents a skill being cancelled by it (prior evidence, dc:52401, unchanged by this batch). No boss-side CC immunities or resistances were found in this batch; whether the boss itself can be lifted, knocked back, or stunned is unresolved (searches for '면역' in this batch returned only unrelated cookie-kit discussion).
boss.death_of_cookies: A cookie reduced to 0 HP is shown greyed out with an hourglass badge in the formation UI and deals no further damage for the rest of the run (dc:74793). No source describes a revive mechanic inside a Guild Conquest attempt; death appears permanent for that attempt.
boss.confidence: medium (element/weakness and the damage-race framing are high confidence from prior evidence; the specific HP/DEF/ATK/DR numbers are low confidence, resting on one unverified poster's self-described datamine)

patterns.timing: Elapsed ~30 s (countdown ~30 s remaining), immediately followed by a distinct mob/add hit around elapsed ~33 s (countdown ~27 s remaining).
patterns.detail: Multi-part: gift-bomb, then ground pounds, then 3 bomb-mobs thrown at the front line (prior evidence dc:53667), then the mob wave detonates a few seconds later. HP floor to survive is roughly 3-4M generally, or front row ~4.5M / back row ~3.5M split by row; team-power curve is roughly 400M power (1-2 survive) -> 600M (whole team survives) -> 1.5G+ (never dies here). RNG-sensitive even at a fixed build.

patterns.timing: Elapsed ~43 s (countdown 17 s remaining); individual deaths taper in from about elapsed ~41 s (countdown 19 s remaining).
patterns.detail: Historically a certain full-team wipe for every publicly documented run except a handful of ~21G-power accounts, where 4 specific cookies (Macaron/Brightseeker/Pomegranate/Skating Queen) have been reported surviving and dealing damage until ~8 s remain (prior evidence, dc:76583/69856/74801). Survival threshold reported at roughly 9M HP + 45% damage reduction per surviving cookie (prior evidence).

patterns.timing: 0-10s: DR 0%; 10-22s: 10%; 22-34s: 30%; 34-46s: 50%; 46-58s: 70%; 58s+: 90%; a 99% stage exists in the data but its 70s start is never reached in a 60s fight.
patterns.detail: Unverified single-poster datamine (dc:67285, refined by the same author in dc:71383); boss ATK is claimed to scale up at the same stage boundaries, from 5,000 to 750,005,000. If real, this explains why chip damage in the first ~10s is comparatively cheap for the team to survive while the 30s and 17s patterns are lethal, and why raw damage output (not just survival) should be front-loaded before defense stacks up. Needs independent confirmation from a client datamine.

scoring.what_counts: Cumulative damage dealt by the team during the 60 s window; a run that wipes entirely well before the timer still keeps and scores the damage already dealt (dc:69201: a full wipe still scored >100x). No source in this batch specifically confirms or denies whether summon/DoT damage (Scorpion poison, Cool Mint's fan, etc.) is included, but crumb.gg's DPS chart (prior evidence, 15-crumbgg/32-dps-read.txt) explicitly counts summon damage 'in full' for its own ranking purposes, which is at least suggestive that the game does the same.
scoring.time_limit: 60 s fixed (see timeline). The fight is not ended early by a team wipe; the clock runs to 0 regardless, and any earlier death simply stops that cookie's contribution.
scoring.result_screen: Not directly captured in this batch beyond the mid-fight damage counter transcribed from dc:76283/74793's screenshots (a running total, not obviously a distinct 'result screen' state). Open question: what the end-of-run result screen actually shows (final score breakdown per cookie? time-of-death log?).

positioning.run_in_behaviour: There is no scripted formation; cookies run in from their configured 12-slot order and physically collide into a line, stopping only when blocked by an ally or the boss. Leftover move-speed stats on any cookie (including pure buffers like Pomegranate) will push it further forward than intended, breaking the tuned line (dc:72759, dc:74804). Removing all backline supports lets a targeted cookie (e.g. Milk) run all the way to melee contact with the boss, at the cost of engaging/dying too early to maximize score (dc:72759).
positioning.charge_type_avoidance: Charge-type (돌격형) cookies are avoided in the Guild Conquest lineup specifically because they always rush into melee range on the boss regardless of the rest of the formation, which both breaks the tuned line and typically puts them outside Milk's ATK-buff range (dc:73560, corroborating prior evidence on why Cherry/Melon Soda are used instead to force a straight line).
positioning.diagnostic_checkpoints: Top players judge whether a run's positioning/buff-landing 'worked' using elapsed-time checkpoints rather than just the final formation: whether Brightseeker and Macaron keep receiving every buff through to the end of the fight, and — for the Jungle Warrior variant — whether Pomegranate's 2-beam upgrade lands by 45 s elapsed and her 3-beam upgrade by 27 s elapsed, and whether Tea Knight receives at least one Pomegranate beam (dc:70056).
positioning.formation_quality_is_not_everything: A visibly poor end-of-fight formation can still land close to a personal-best score, implying formation is one of several score-driving factors (alongside crit RNG and buff-timing luck) rather than the single deciding one (dc:74887).

buff_mechanics.title: Pomegranate beam-count timing checkpoints
buff_mechanics.body: For the Jungle Warrior variant specifically, a top player's own diagnostic requires Pomegranate's beam count to step up to 2 multi-hit stacks by 45 s elapsed and to 3 stacks by 27 s elapsed, plus Tea Knight receiving at least one beam, as evidence a run's positioning/buff landing was good (not just the final ATK order).

buff_mechanics.title: Milk's death window from the 30s slam removes her buff for the rest of the fight
buff_mechanics.body: Because Milk is often occupied healing teammates during the 30s slam and isn't healed herself, she can die at that pattern even when lower-HP fillers survive it — creating an observed ~11 s gap (28s to 17s remaining) with no ATK buff active before the final wipe finishes the run.

buff_mechanics.title: Buffers still need move-speed zeroed, not just positioning
buff_mechanics.body: A pure buffer (Pomegranate) with leftover move-speed stats will run forward into the wrong position even in an otherwise-tuned Cherry deck; the practical fix used is stripping move speed entirely rather than relying on formation order alone.

buff_mechanics.title: Score doesn't require survival to the buzzer
buff_mechanics.body: Damage dealt before a cookie's or team's death is retained; a full wipe at the 30s slam can still score over 100x. This confirms score = cumulative damage over the 60s clock, not a pass/fail tied to reaching any checkpoint.

open_questions: Independent confirmation of the boss's DR/ATK/DEF/HP datamine numbers (dc:67285/67299/71383) — this rests on one poster's self-described, admittedly uncertain client datamine with no screenshot evidence. A real client extraction should look for a boss stat table / status-effect table keyed to the Guild Conquest stage id (something like a 'GuildRaid boss phase' or 'BossPhaseCondition' data row gated on elapsed battle time, given the '10s then every 12s' cadence described).

Whether the 27s mob-wave hit (dc:71219, dc:67659) is a fixed, separately-named pattern in the game's own data, or just community shorthand for the tail end of the '30s slam' sequence described in prior evidence (dc:53667: gift-bomb -> ground pounds -> 3 bomb-mobs -> jump). Look for a distinct skill/pattern id firing a few seconds after the id likely responsible for the 30s hit.

Whether the boss ever moves toward, chases, or selects a specific cookie target, or whether all its patterns are untargeted AoE hitting whoever is in range/front line. No source in this project describes boss movement or single-target boss attacks.
Whether the boss itself has any CC immunities (lift, knockback, stun) or whether it can be lifted/staggered by ally skills — not found in any source to date.
Whether summon/pet/DoT damage (Scorpion poison ticks, Cool Mint fan hits, etc.) counts toward the Guild Conquest score the same way crumb.gg's DPS chart counts them for its own ranking purposes.
What the actual post-fight result screen shows (per-cookie damage breakdown? time of each death? just a total?) — not captured in any source read so far.

Exact 12-slot formation-to-screen-position mapping (which of the 12 list positions in crumb.gg's simulator corresponds to which physical row/column in the actual fight) — crumb.gg's own simulator UI confirms the ordered 12-slot list exists but doesn't expose the physical layout.

Whether a cookie that dies can ever be revived mid-run by any Guild-Conquest-legal effect — no evidence found either way beyond the observed 'downed' UI state and the assumption (from every survival-focused post read) that death is permanent for that attempt.

The likely underlying data to search for in a client datamine, by name: a 'GuildRaid' or 'GuildConquest' boss definition table with a phase/stage array keyed on elapsed time (matching the claimed 10s-then-12s cadence); a boss pattern/skill table with cast-time fields for whatever ids drive the 30s and 17s hits; and a 'DamageReductionByPhase' or similar stat-modifier table on the boss's status-effect definitions.
